# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Open-ear buds leave your ears uncovered, so you can hear traffic and other runners. Reviewers still say to keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299).** Runner's World picks them as its best overall, citing excellent audio and a comfortable clip design. RTINGS rates them slightly better than the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 for most people, because they're more portable, more stable and don't press on your temples. They're expensive, and Immersive Audio can glitch. [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list.** WIRED's review (Aug 2024) found it a great fit for running with big sound for bone conduction. Its drawbacks are IP55 water resistance (sweat-proof, not swim-proof) and battery life shorter than promised. WIRED listed it at $125 at REI and Best Buy, but that was in the 2024 review, so check current pricing. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

- **Best for long runs and all-weather use: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200.** WIRED's top open-earbud pick has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case), an IP57 rating and a clip-on design that leaves the top of your ear free for glasses or a hat. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

- **Best value: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 (list $149).** SoundGuys names it best overall among open-ear models, and it also picks it as best for running among workout earbuds. [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) · [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

- **Best budget hook-style: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has an IP55 rating, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), a 4-position adjustable hook and 10 g buds. SoundGuys lists it at **$79.99 on Amazon** and calls it the best budget pick. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**A note on the AeroFit 2 price:** A deal site, Dealectric, lists code AFSC20 as taking $25.99 off a $129.99 price at Soundcore's store, for $104 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)). That's an affiliate page, and the SoundGuys Amazon price above is lower even before any code. Compare both at checkout before buying.

**How to choose**

- **Maximum awareness, and you're fine with a neckband:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. Bone conduction leaves your ears the most open.
- **Most comfortable and best sound:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Rain, sweat and long distances:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** Nothing Ear (Open) or Soundcore AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs leak sound and offer no isolation, so they're poor for loud gyms or planes. If you tell me your budget and whether you use an iPhone or Android, I can narrow it to one.
